name: Auth0
summary: Auth0 is a managed identity platform run by Okta; Authorizer is an open-source server you run yourself, with your users in your own database.

rows.authorizer: Open source, Apache-2.0
rows.them: Proprietary, closed-source service

rows.authorizer: Self-hosted: one Go binary or Docker image you run on your own infrastructure
rows.them: Not self-hostable: Public Cloud and Private Cloud deployments are managed by Auth0

rows.authorizer: Free and open source; you pay only for the infrastructure you run it on
rows.them: Paid plans priced by monthly active users (MAU)

rows.authorizer: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect provider (authorization code + PKCE, client credentials, refresh, discovery, JWKS)
rows.them: OAuth 2.1 / OIDC

rows.authorizer: Per-organization SAML 2.0 as Service Provider and as Identity Provider
rows.them: SAML as Identity Provider, Service Provider, or both

rows.authorizer: Per-organization inbound SCIM 2.0 (RFC 7644)
rows.them: Inbound SCIM 2.0; requires Enterprise Connections on your plan

rows.authorizer: Embedded OpenFGA (Zanzibar-style ReBAC) in the same binary, including conditional, time-limited grants
rows.them: Auth0 FGA, a separate hosted ReBAC product based on OpenFGA

rows.authorizer: Built-in MCP server; RFC 8693 delegation where every check requires both the agent and the user; RFC 9728 / RFC 8707 / Client ID Metadata Documents
rows.them: Auth for MCP and On-Behalf-Of token exchange; agent identity in tokens is in Early Access; Auth0 for AI Agents is a paid add-on

themFit: Teams that want a fully managed CIAM platform with enterprise SSO and SCIM, and accept Auth0-hosted deployment only.

name: Clerk
summary: Clerk is a hosted authentication service with prebuilt UI components; Authorizer is an open-source server you self-host, with its own login UI and headless APIs.

rows.authorizer: Open source, Apache-2.0
rows.them: SDKs are MIT-licensed; the service itself is not open source

rows.authorizer: Self-hosted: one Go binary or Docker image you run on your own infrastructure
rows.them: No self-hosted option is listed

rows.authorizer: Free and open source; you pay only for the infrastructure you run it on
rows.them: Billed on retained users (MRU), not MAU

rows.authorizer: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect provider (authorization code + PKCE, client credentials, refresh, discovery, JWKS)
rows.them: Acts as an OAuth 2.0 / OIDC authorization server

rows.authorizer: Per-organization SAML 2.0 as Service Provider and as Identity Provider
rows.them: SAML for enterprise SSO (as Service Provider)

rows.authorizer: Per-organization inbound SCIM 2.0 (RFC 7644)
rows.them: SCIM 2.0 Directory Sync on Pro and Business plans

rows.authorizer: Embedded OpenFGA (Zanzibar-style ReBAC) in the same binary, including conditional, time-limited grants
rows.them: Organization roles and custom permissions

rows.authorizer: Built-in MCP server; RFC 8693 delegation where every check requires both the agent and the user; RFC 9728 / RFC 8707 / Client ID Metadata Documents
rows.them: Guide for building an MCP server with Clerk OAuth, RFC 9728 metadata and Client ID Metadata Documents

themFit: JavaScript and React apps that want hosted auth with prebuilt UI components and B2B organizations.

name: Keycloak
summary: Keycloak and Authorizer are both open source and self-hosted. Keycloak is a Java (Quarkus) IAM server; Authorizer is a single Go binary with OpenFGA and an MCP server built in.

rows.authorizer: Open source, Apache-2.0
rows.them: Open source, Apache-2.0

rows.authorizer: Self-hosted: one Go binary or Docker image you run on your own infrastructure
rows.them: Self-hosted; Red Hat offers no managed Keycloak service

rows.authorizer: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect provider (authorization code + PKCE, client credentials, refresh, discovery, JWKS)
rows.them: OpenID Connect and OAuth 2.0

rows.authorizer: Per-organization SAML 2.0 as Service Provider and as Identity Provider
rows.them: SAML Identity Provider and SAML identity brokering

rows.authorizer: Per-organization inbound SCIM 2.0 (RFC 7644)
rows.them: SCIM API is experimental (26.6, behind the scim-api feature flag)

rows.authorizer: Embedded OpenFGA (Zanzibar-style ReBAC) in the same binary, including conditional, time-limited grants
rows.them: Built-in Authorization Services: role-, attribute-, user- and context-based policies and UMA

rows.authorizer: Built-in MCP server; RFC 8693 delegation where every check requires both the agent and the user; RFC 9728 / RFC 8707 / Client ID Metadata Documents
rows.them: MCP authorization-server guide (newer MCP spec features experimental); RFC 8693 token exchange enabled by default

themFit: Organizations that want a mature, self-operated, Java-based IAM with SAML and identity federation.

name: SuperTokens
summary: SuperTokens has an open-source core with managed and licensed add-ons; Authorizer is fully Apache-2.0, with SAML, SCIM and fine-grained authorization in the open-source server.

rows.authorizer: Open source, Apache-2.0
rows.them: Core is Apache-2.0; the ee/ directory is under the proprietary SuperTokens Enterprise License

rows.authorizer: Self-hosted: one Go binary or Docker image you run on your own infrastructure
rows.them: Partially: some features need a license key, and the OAuth2 provider (unified login) is not in the self-hosted version

rows.authorizer: Free and open source; you pay only for the infrastructure you run it on
rows.them: Priced per monthly active user (MAU), with paid add-ons

rows.authorizer: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect provider (authorization code + PKCE, client credentials, refresh, discovery, JWKS)
rows.them: OAuth2 provider is managed-only

rows.authorizer: Per-organization SAML 2.0 as Service Provider and as Identity Provider
rows.them: SAML as Service Provider, a paid feature

rows.authorizer: Embedded OpenFGA (Zanzibar-style ReBAC) in the same binary, including conditional, time-limited grants
rows.them: User roles and permissions

rows.authorizer: Built-in MCP server; RFC 8693 delegation where every check requires both the agent and the user; RFC 9728 / RFC 8707 / Client ID Metadata Documents
rows.them: MCP authentication in beta, Node SDK only, managed-only

themFit: Apps that want an embeddable auth layer with an open-source core and managed add-ons.

name: Zitadel
summary: Zitadel and Authorizer are both Go servers you can self-host. Zitadel is AGPL-3.0 and also offered as SaaS; Authorizer is Apache-2.0 and adds embedded OpenFGA and an MCP server.

rows.authorizer: Open source, Apache-2.0
rows.them: AGPL-3.0 (some components Apache-2.0 or MIT)

rows.authorizer: Self-hosted: one Go binary or Docker image you run on your own infrastructure
rows.them: Self-hostable (Docker Compose, Kubernetes/Helm; requires PostgreSQL) and available as managed cloud

rows.authorizer: Free and open source; you pay only for the infrastructure you run it on
rows.them: Managed cloud priced per daily active user (DAU)

rows.authorizer: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect provider (authorization code + PKCE, client credentials, refresh, discovery, JWKS)
rows.them: OpenID Connect certified

rows.authorizer: Per-organization SAML 2.0 as Service Provider and as Identity Provider
rows.them: SAML 2.0 Identity Provider (SP-initiated) and external SAML identity providers

rows.authorizer: Per-organization inbound SCIM 2.0 (RFC 7644)
rows.them: SCIM 2.0 server

rows.authorizer: Embedded OpenFGA (Zanzibar-style ReBAC) in the same binary, including conditional, time-limited grants
rows.them: Roles and delegated project grants

rows.authorizer: Built-in MCP server; RFC 8693 delegation where every check requires both the agent and the user; RFC 9728 / RFC 8707 / Client ID Metadata Documents
rows.them: RFC 8693 token exchange and impersonation; AI-agent identity patterns guide

themFit: Multi-tenant B2B identity, either self-hosted under AGPL or used as SaaS.

name: Ory
summary: Ory is a set of composable services (Kratos, Hydra, Keto) plus Ory Network; Authorizer puts authentication, OAuth/OIDC, enterprise SSO and OpenFGA authorization in one binary.

rows.authorizer: Open source, Apache-2.0
rows.them: Kratos, Hydra, Keto and Polis are Apache-2.0; SAML, SCIM and organization SSO need the commercial Ory Enterprise License

rows.authorizer: Self-hosted: one Go binary or Docker image you run on your own infrastructure
rows.them: Open-source components are self-hostable; some enterprise features are not in the open-source version

rows.authorizer: Free and open source; you pay only for the infrastructure you run it on
rows.them: Ory Network priced per average daily active user (aDAU)

rows.authorizer: OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect provider (authorization code + PKCE, client credentials, refresh, discovery, JWKS)
rows.them: Ory Hydra is an OpenID-certified OAuth 2.0 / OIDC provider

rows.authorizer: Per-organization SAML 2.0 as Service Provider and as Identity Provider
rows.them: SAML Service Provider on select Enterprise plans

rows.authorizer: Per-organization inbound SCIM 2.0 (RFC 7644)
rows.them: Organization-level SCIM on Ory Network

rows.authorizer: Embedded OpenFGA (Zanzibar-style ReBAC) in the same binary, including conditional, time-limited grants
rows.them: Ory Keto, an open-source Zanzibar (ReBAC) implementation, also offered as Ory Network Permissions

rows.authorizer: Built-in MCP server; RFC 8693 delegation where every check requires both the agent and the user; RFC 9728 / RFC 8707 / Client ID Metadata Documents
rows.them: Guide to OAuth 2.1 for MCP with Hydra or Ory Network

themFit: Teams that want composable, API-first identity components, self-hosted or on Ory Network.
